admission.justification: A held `j` can outrun the answer that brings the next family. "No later change in this tree" then stands beside a later change and tells the reader the walk is over when it is not. A status cleared by an update made while rendering comes back, because React can apply a queued status after that render. The rule is realized in the traversal hook and in the tree component, and a case on the hook alone and mounted cases guard it.

applicability: The j/k block traversal status of the review page.
conditions: The status key is the ordered key sequence of actual drawn block stops, including lane hunk stops.
The first render with a different stop key gates out the old status and a layout effect clears it; rendering updates no status state.
Repeating the same message for the same stop key is a no-op; a selected stop clears the status, and an end retains the selection.
exclusions: Tree-only filter/view changes that preserve the same actual stops do not promise status invalidation.
Continuation groups are places rather than traversal stops.
statement: A traversal end message is shown only for the ordered drawn block stops it described; once different stops have been shown it is cleared and does not return when the same stops return.
